topStories.headline: A 20-Foot Steel Sculpture Has Landed in the Middle of Alamo Square Park
topStories.dek: The artist duo HYBYCOZO installed 'Axis Mundi' on October 15 as part of the Big Art Loop public art trail — and it will stay for a full year.
topStories.body:
A striking new sculpture now stands at the center of Alamo Square Park, where it joins the neighborhood's Victorian skyline and the sight lines toward downtown. The piece, titled 'Axis Mundi,' was installed on October 15 by San Francisco-based artist duo HYBYCOZO — Serge Beaulieu and Yelena Filipchuk — as part of the Big Art Loop, a citywide initiative placing large-scale temporary sculptures along a 34-mile walkable and bikeable route across San Francisco.

The work measures 20 feet tall and is fabricated from powder-coated steel with LED lighting, according to the SF Arts Commission agenda item that approved the installation. The SF Arts Commission's Visual Arts Committee approved the placement in coordination with the San Francisco Recreation and Parks Department. The commission authorized a one-year loan of the piece, meaning it will remain in the park through roughly October 2027.

HYBYCOZO's geometric sculptures are designed to read differently by day and by night: the latticed steel forms cast lacy shadow patterns in sunlight, while LED lights animate the structure after dark — making the park a new evening destination for neighbors who pass through. Big Art Loop celebrated the installation with a community picnic at Alamo Square on the evening of the unveiling, inviting residents to bring their own food and meet the artists.

The Big Art Loop project describes itself as the largest urban sculpture trail in the world and is currently placing works in parks across all five segments of the route. The budget for 'Axis Mundi' at Alamo Square is listed at $154,700, which covers artist fees, engineering, installation, and ongoing maintenance — all free to the public, with no ticket or reservation required.

topStories.headline: Greystar Breaks Ground This Week on the Long-Stalled Divisadero Car Wash Site
topStories.dek: Construction logistics are now active at 400 Divisadero — the Oak and Divisadero sidewalks are closed and a lane is occupied — as the decade-long saga of the former Touchless Car Wash moves into its building phase.
topStories.body:
The intersection of Divisadero and Oak streets looks different this week. Sidewalk closures are in effect on both the Divisadero and Oak frontages of 400 Divisadero, and a portion of an Oak Street traffic lane is now occupied by a construction staging zone. San Francisco Public Works issued the permits for those closures with an October 19 start date — meaning the long-delayed, long-debated redevelopment of the former Touchless Car Wash site has crossed from planning into physical reality.

The developer behind the move is Greystar, the largest apartment developer in the United States by portfolio, which acquired the project from 4Terra Investments earlier this year after securing the financing needed to absorb the entitlement risk that had repeatedly stalled the project. The plan calls for an eight-story mixed-use building with 203 apartments — 121 one-bedrooms and 82 two-bedrooms — along with roughly 1,850 square feet of ground-floor retail and 24 parking stalls. Twenty of the 203 units are deed-restricted affordable housing.

The site at Divisadero and Oak has been tied up in proposals, political disputes, and regulatory delays since at least 2017, cycling through multiple developers and building-code revisions that added an estimated 5 to 7 percent to construction costs each time the project restarted. A key legislative fix — the SHADE Act, championed by District 5 Supervisor Bilal Mahmood — allowed the project to use the building code in effect when it first applied rather than being forced to comply with successive updates. The project received ministerial approval under AB 2011 in late 2024.

A separate demolition permit for the car wash structure itself was still awaiting final approval as of the Chronicle's August report, but the public-works street permits confirm that construction logistics are already underway. The eight-story building, designed by BDE Architecture, will include a podium-top central courtyard, a rooftop terrace, and bicycle storage for 144 bikes.

topStories.headline: Hayes Street Closure Debate Intensifies as HVNA Hosts Transportation and Safety Forum
topStories.dek: The Hayes Valley Neighborhood Association held a public meeting Thursday night on transportation and safety, even as the city's SF Planning 'Public Life Study' on the Hayes Street closure draws competing visions for the corridor's future.
topStories.body:
The Hayes Valley Neighborhood Association held a joint transportation and safety meeting on Thursday, October 22, at 6:30 p.m. — a community forum at which residents could hear updates and raise concerns about traffic, pedestrian safety, and the contested closure of the 400 block of Hayes Street.

The meeting arrived at a pointed moment in the ongoing debate over what Hayes Street should ultimately become. SFMTA is currently closing the block every Friday from 4 to 10 p.m. and every Saturday from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. for the Hayes Valley Farmers Market and Shared Spaces event, with the outbound 6 Hayes/Parnassus Muni route rerouted onto Grove Street during closure hours. The closures are permitted through the end of 2026.

At the same time, SF Planning is conducting a 'Public Life Study' of the corridor, and the Hayes Valley Merchants Council September newsletter encouraged businesses to complete the planning department's survey. The HVNA — which holds the permit for the existing Shared Spaces closure, marketed as Hayes Promenade — has described its long-term goal as creating a permanently 'pedestrian-forward model of Hayes Street,' not just a recurring weekly closure. That framing has drawn pushback from the advocacy group Hayes Valley Safe, which has documented ongoing permit-compliance concerns at the closure site and has questioned whether the planning process is being conducted neutrally.

The UC Berkeley College of Environmental Design published a study earlier this year that found the Hayes Promenade strengthens community, local businesses, and public life — a finding cited by closure supporters. Critics counter that the research was designed to support continuation of the closure rather than evaluate it independently. SF Planning's survey remains open to residents and businesses in the area.

events.title: Big Art Loop October Walking Challenge
events.location: Big Art Loop, citywide (Alamo Square segment, NoPa)
events.description: Big Art Loop is challenging residents to explore the trail one short walk at a time throughout October. The newly installed 'Axis Mundi' by HYBYCOZO at Alamo Square Park is a featured stop on the North City segment; free and accessible 24/7.

events.description: The North of Panhandle Neighborhood Association's regular monthly cleanup. Meet at Hayes and Central; supplies provided. One of NOPNA's recurring community-building events, held on the fourth Saturday of each month.

events.title: NOPNA Fourth Friday Happy Hour
events.description: NOPNA's monthly casual neighborhood social, held on the fourth Friday of each month. Venue announced via the NOPNA Instagram and newsletter; check their site for the confirmed location.

moreNews.headline: ASNA Confirms It Funds Trees for Alamo Square Park's Urban Forest
moreNews.body: The Alamo Square Neighborhood Association published a note on September 30 reminding residents that ASNA directly purchases trees planted in Alamo Square Park as part of a long-term commitment to the park's urban forest. The post outlines the association's ongoing role in maintaining and expanding the park's tree canopy — a detail that takes on added significance now that the park also hosts the new 'Axis Mundi' sculpture from Big Art Loop. ASNA's next board meeting is scheduled for November 10 at 6:30 p.m. at The Archbishop's Mansion, 1000 Fulton Street.

moreNews.headline: NOPNA Community Meeting Set for November 19
moreNews.body: The North of Panhandle Neighborhood Association holds its bi-monthly community meeting on the third Thursday of every other month. The next gathering is scheduled for Thursday, November 19, at Brahma Kumaris. Meetings typically feature city officials, neighborhood Q&A, and trivia. The October date fell in a non-meeting month; November 19 is the next opportunity for residents to hear directly from city representatives about issues affecting NoPa.

restaurants.name: Rich Table
restaurants.description: Husband-and-wife chefs Evan and Sarah Rich serve hyper-seasonal, inventive California cuisine in a lively Hayes Valley dining room — one of SF's toughest reservations since 2012.

restaurants.name: RT Bistro
restaurants.description: The more casual, 37-seat sister spot to Rich Table — opened early 2026 next door — featuring the RT Bistro burger, one-layer lasagna, and a crowd-pleasing bistro menu.

restaurants.name: RT Rotisserie
restaurants.description: The Rich Table team's fast-casual offshoot focused on rotisserie chicken and home-style seasonal dishes, open daily in Hayes Valley.

restaurants.name: Nightbird

restaurants.name: Absinthe Brasserie & Bar

restaurants.name: Zuni Café
restaurants.description: A San Francisco institution since 1979, Zuni occupies a triangular Market Street building and is legendary for its wood-fired roast chicken and brick-oven cooking.

restaurants.name: Suppenküche
restaurants.description: Hayes Valley's beloved Bavarian Wirthaus since 1993, offering hearty German classics like schnitzel, pretzels, and an exceptional specialty beer list.

restaurants.name: Dumpling Home
restaurants.description: Michelin Bib Gourmand-recognized Hayes Valley spot serving hand-folded xiao long bao (soup dumplings), pan-fried buns, and other Chinese classics.

restaurants.name: Hazie's
restaurants.description: A stylish Hayes Valley restaurant praised for its cocktails, happy hour, and modern American dinner menu in a comfortable neighborhood setting.

restaurants.name: Souvla
restaurants.description: The original Hayes Valley location of this beloved Greek fast-casual chain, known for rotisserie meats, big salads, and a sunny backyard patio.

restaurants.name: Chez Maman West
restaurants.description: A cozy Hayes Valley French bistro serving classics like steak frites, mussels, and crêpes in a lively street-side setting.

restaurants.name: Smuggler's Cove
restaurants.description: A three-story Hayes Valley tiki bar with more than 1,300 varieties of rum — the largest selection of any bar in the US — and a 80-cocktail menu of tiki classics and originals.

restaurants.name: Nopa
restaurants.description: The neighborhood namesake at 560 Divisadero has served organic wood-fired California cuisine with a daily-changing menu since 2006, remaining one of SF's most beloved dining rooms.

restaurants.name: Bar Crudo
restaurants.description: A vibrant NoPa raw bar specializing in creative crudo, fresh oysters, and sustainably sourced seafood, with a popular happy hour running Monday through Saturday.

restaurants.name: Horsefeather
restaurants.type: Cocktail bar and New American restaurant
restaurants.description: A reliably good NoPa cocktail bar and restaurant with inventive drinks, fried chicken, duck fat fries, and a warm Arts-and-Crafts-inspired interior open late nightly.

restaurants.name: Brenda's Meat & Three
restaurants.description: New Orleans–born chef Brenda Buenviaje's NoPa diner lets diners choose one meat and three sides from a rotating array of down-home Southern classics, with a legendary breakfast menu.

restaurants.name: Nopalito
restaurants.description: Chef Gonzalo Guzmán's original Broderick Street location — open since 2009 — serving blue-corn tacos, carnitas, and seasonal Mexican dishes rooted in Veracruz family cooking.

restaurants.name: Altamirano Restaurant & Bar
restaurants.description: A spacious NoPa Peruvian restaurant with an exhibition kitchen, a lively bar, and an outdoor courtyard with a fire pit for dining al fresco.

hotels.name: Hayes Valley Inn
hotels.description: A well-located, affordable 2-star inn on Gough Street in the heart of Hayes Valley, offering easy access to the neighborhood's restaurants, shops, and performing arts venues.

hotels.name: The Grove Inn
hotels.description: A family-owned Italianate-Victorian style inn in the heart of the Alamo Square Historic District, operating for over four decades and continuing a legacy dating to 1865.

hotels.name: Symphony Inn
hotels.description: A well-maintained budget motel in Hayes Valley, conveniently located near City Hall and the performing arts district with easy access to neighborhood restaurants.

hotels.name: Inn at the Opera
hotels.description: An intimate boutique hotel ideally located in the Performing Arts District near Hayes Valley, catering to opera, symphony, and ballet patrons.

hotels.name: Casa Loma Hotel
hotels.description: A European-style budget hotel near Hayes Valley offering affordable accommodation with easy access to public transit and the neighborhood's dining scene.

shops.name: Métier

shops.name: AETHER Apparel

shops.name: Cotton Sheep

shops.name: Marine Layer
shops.description: Hayes Valley outpost of the popular SF-founded brand, offering signature soft knits, sweatshirts, and tees made from cotton-modal blends.

shops.name: Peak Design
shops.type: Camera and travel gear flagship store
shops.description: The flagship Hayes Valley store for the SF-based Peak Design, selling bags, camera straps, tripods, and everyday carry gear in a beautifully designed retail space.

shops.name: The Epicurean Trader
shops.description: A curated Hayes Valley shop stocking artisan provisions, craft beer, wine, and spirits alongside an in-house coffee bar.

shops.name: Fiddlesticks
shops.description: A cheerful Hayes Street children's boutique stocked with colorful clothing, toys, and books, blending playful design with durable quality.

shops.name: Bulo Shoes
shops.description: A well-regarded Hayes Street shoe boutique carrying a carefully edited selection of European and independent footwear brands.

shops.name: minimal

shops.name: Azil Boutique

artEntertainment.name: SFJAZZ Center
artEntertainment.type: Jazz and world music concert hall
artEntertainment.description: The first stand-alone structure in the US built specifically for jazz, SFJAZZ presents more than 100 concerts a year in the Robert N. Miner Auditorium and the 100-seat Joe Henderson Lab at the corner of Franklin and Fell streets.

artEntertainment.name: Orpheum Theatre
artEntertainment.description: A 2,197-seat San Francisco landmark theater dating to 1926, operated by ATG Entertainment (BroadwaySF), hosting major Broadway touring productions on Market Street.

artEntertainment.description: Opened in 2017, this nonprofit gallery and printmaking studio at 215 Haight Street celebrates the history and cultural impact of poster art, with free rotating exhibitions open Thursday–Sunday.

artEntertainment.name: Hayes Valley Art Works
artEntertainment.description: A converted shipping-container gallery at Oak and Octavia operated by the Hayes Valley Neighborhood Association, hosting exhibitions, monthly Jazz Jams, weekend workshops, and a community garden.

artEntertainment.name: Alamo Square Park
